note: Families I-VIII were declared in v1 and v3; IX and X are numbered here for the first time, without renumbering any existing id. Family XI (collective action, prefix L) is numbered in v9, again without renumbering any existing id. SCOPE (operator ruling, 2026-09-02): the taxonomy includes ALL AGENTIC SOURCES and is REPOSITORY-INDEPENDENT. The classes describe how oversight of agentic work fails, not how one codebase fails, so an instance qualifies on its mechanism and never on where it was found — instances from clientDRemote, overwatch-layer and memory-layer are already held, and an instance from a repository this fleet has never touched qualifies equally. The requirement is attribution, not provenance: every instance names the repo and the session that measured it, because an instance from one population recorded as if it came from another is M1. An earlier version of this line said "fleet-scoped", which was my inference from what had been folded rather than a stated policy; it was narrower than the truth and is corrected here. FAMILIES CARRY A MEMBERSHIP TEST from 2026-09-07: the sentence a second rater applies to decide whether a class belongs, in the same form the stpa, rca and mitigation vocabularies already require. Added after family VI was measured as the one family whose members are more like another family's than like each other; a family that declares only a proposition cannot refuse a member. The tests are DECLARED, not enforced against existing membership, because moving a class renumbers it and breaks every citation.

intro.public: AI coding agents fail most dangerously when the failure looks like success — a clean report over work nobody checked, a fix that silenced the alarm instead of the fault, a record crediting the wrong author — and this page names every such failure we have measured, one row each, with the incident that earned it its place.
intro.academic: Formally, it is a registry of oversight-failure classes for agentic LLM systems: each class is a falsifiable predicate over artefacts, bound to an STPA control loop, an unsafe-control-action type and a causal factor, scored for closure and residual gain, and linked to its neighbours by a closed set of causal relations, so that inter-rater agreement, coverage and drift are measurable rather than asserted.

families.name: False clean
families.test: The subject is reported as having nothing wrong with it, and that clean reading is indistinguishable from the one a check would produce if it had never run, never reached the subject, or could not have failed. The defect is in the CLEAN READING. A row whose finding exists and is merely wrong belongs to family II.

families.name: False alarm content
families.proposition: and this is what is wrong / what to do
families.test: Something fired and published a finding, and the finding misstates its own subject, scope, cause or applicability. The alarm is REAL: what is wrong is what it says about the world. A row where nothing fired at all belongs to family I.

families.name: False repair
families.test: A repair, guard or remediation is in place and is credited with a property it does not have, because it cannot run, runs over less than it claims, or changed only what a detector matched. The row requires an ATTEMPTED FIX to exist; a defect nobody has tried to repair belongs elsewhere.

families.name: False provenance
families.test: A record names who or what produced something, or is consumed as if it did, and the naming is not supported by what that record can actually observe. The subject is AUTHORSHIP or OWNERSHIP. A row about whether a number is right belongs to family V.

families.name: False measurement
families.proposition: and this number means what it says
families.test: A published quantity, comparison, denominator or scope is arithmetically and procedurally sound, and does not measure the thing its consumer reads it as measuring. The subject is a NUMBER or a comparison, and the arithmetic is not in dispute.

families.name: Model-generated defect
families.proposition: and the agent's own output is usable
families.test: The defect is IN what a model produced or in the judgement a model issued, and it is present in that artefact itself. NOT an origin test: because the register's scope ruling makes every class here a description of agentic work, "an agent was involved" admits almost any row and cannot refuse anything. Membership requires the model's OUTPUT to be the defective thing, not merely the circumstance in which some other defect was found. Rows about how agents are SCORED belong to the family of the thing being mis-scored.

families.name: False durability
families.proposition: and this record will still be there
families.test: Something was written, recorded, cited or stored, and it does not survive to the moment, the surface or the reader it was written for. The subject is SURVIVAL over time or across a boundary; the content was correct when it was written.

families.name: False progress
families.proposition: and this turn advanced the work
families.test: A session's own activity reads as progress and the work did not advance. The subject is the AGENT'S EXPENDITURE, never the artefact it produced. A defective artefact belongs to the family its defect names.

families.name: False control
families.proposition: and the deciding layer was in a position to decide it
families.test: A controller, scheduler or gate is in the loop, and the decision credited to it was not made by it, was made and not carried out, or was made over a state it does not govern. The subject is the CONTROL RELATION, not the correctness of any single act.

families.name: Imported defect
families.proposition: and the components and rules I depend on are the ones I validated
families.test: The defect arrives with a third-party instrument, vendor result, dependency or adopted taxonomy, and this system's own code is correct throughout. Removing the import removes the defect. A row where our own handling of a sound import is at fault belongs elsewhere.

families.name: Collective action
families.proposition: and each of these actors decided on its own
families.test: Every actor behaved correctly on the evidence it individually held, and the failure exists only in the RELATION between them. No single actor's behaviour, corrected alone, removes it. A row that one actor could have prevented by acting differently is not collective.

classes.name: Absence rendered as success
classes.description: Not-scanned, no-data or no-file is displayed as clean or fresh.
classes.predicate: A renderer or reducer maps missing/undefined/ENOENT onto a success token (0, [], 'clean', 'ok') with no distinct absent state.

Every push since the secret lapsed on 2026-08-05 ran the job, deployed nothing and showed a tick. Fixed c891c48 by removing the env block and asserting on "Successfully deployed" in the output rather than on the exit code. Measured instance, cra/soc2.mjs 2026-09-24: SOC 2 CC7.4, respond to identified security incidents, carried evidenced: true as a literal, so a product with no case and no recorded risk decision rendered 'evidence present' beside an evidence line reading 0 and 0, in a packet documented as feeding an audit (audit finding 0003). classes.name: Tooling self-deception
classes.description: The measuring instrument lies in a way that specifically produces a clean reading: a search suppresses matches, a probe reads the wrong field. M3 is the general form, including instruments that lie loud rather than quiet.
classes.predicate: Two independent instruments over the same input disagree, or a probe reads a field the source never emits.
classes.example: Under a C locale, grep withheld matching lines in bin/bola-run.mjs while grep -c still counted them, producing four consecutive false "this symbol is gone" conclusions. Second instance, where the control is the finding: sweeping ~/.claude for three identity strings with rg returned 0 files for all three, because rg skips hidden and ignored paths by default and ~/.claude is hidden. Control terms on the identical command shape returned 4,820, 4,105 and 2,290 files, which is the only reason the zero was disbelieved; re-run with -uuu gave 527, 1,349 and 2,184. A published 0/0/0 against a true 527/1,349/2,184. Third instance, and a third mechanism — config-root resolution rather than a search filter: in clientD (Portll/clientDRemote, NOT this repo), a `// deno-lint-ignore react-no-danger` suppression was verified by copying the file to /tmp and running `deno lint` on the copy, which reported "Checked 1 file", 0 findings. deno lint resolves config by walking up from the TARGET file, so from /tmp the site's deno.json never loaded and the fresh-tagged rule was never enabled. Byte-identical file via cp: `deno lint /tmp/copy.tsx` gave 0 findings while `deno lint routes/_app.tsx` from the site root gave 3 problems including error[react-no-danger] at routes/_app.tsx:84:14. The 0 meant the rule did not run, and "Checked 1 file" is the same string either way.
classes.analogy: A broken thermometer reads 37 in every room, so nobody in the ward has a fever.
classes.scoreBasis: discipline only (grep -a, contract-tested clients, and running a linter from the root its config resolves from); no mechanical guard Measured by reporter #4 2026-09-02. Third instance measured by reporter #29 in clientD 2026-09-03 and routed here after reporter #22 went offline; they argued the off-diagonals themselves: not M3, because deno lint is not defective and reports correctly at the real path, and M3's own text puts the false-clean case here; not R3, because coverage was complete over SUBJECTS and the shortfall was in RULES, with the file count accurate. K13 is a defensible alternative they raised and declined to argue for — there a setting moves the root under a stationary control, here the artifact left a stationary root. RE-RATED 2026-09-06 by reporter #3: closure 2→1, gain 3→3. Discipline with no mechanical guard is 1 on the rubric this pass applies — the same level as the W-family sensors — and a third instance arrived 2026-09-03.

classes.name: Attribution to an untouched subject
classes.description: A ledger records an event against a subject the event never touched, so lookup returns nothing for the real one and names an innocent one instead. An absence is recoverable by looking elsewhere; a confident wrong name is not, because nothing prompts the reader to look.
classes.predicate: An attribution event names a subject absent from the event's writes while omitting at least one subject the same event demonstrably changed.
classes.example: touches.jsonl recorded x:"admin/serve.mjs" for a shell heredoc that edited sitemap/README.md. Fixed 2026-09-01 at a commit. Second denominator over the same defect, measured independently: mine.txt 692 rows, s.sh 202, new.sh 200, new.txt 199 — about 1,293 rows carrying via:"commit" with content hashes, for files that exist nowhere in the repository. a commit's own subject states the magnitude: "a third of it was test fixtures, and one gate read them as your edits."

classes.name: Stale by the time it is used
classes.description: Correct when taken, invalid when acted on.
classes.predicate: A record consumed by a decision with no freshness bound, where the record asserts something OBSERVED AT A PAST MOMENT — a measurement, or a capability claim such as "this check has been seen to fail". Includes records carrying NO TIMESTAMP AT ALL, which is the harder case: with nothing to compare against, no freshness bound is expressible and the staleness is undetectable rather than merely unchecked. Decidable by asking what would invalidate the record and whether the consumer can observe it — elapsed time, or a change to the subject the record is about.
classes.example: Six minutes of measurement in one morning saw three different HEADs and a failing set that changed twice. Measured instance in this registry's own read path: the SQLite projection reported 179 classes while the JSON source held 188, in the same minute on 2026-09-02, and the documented `taxonomy-db.mjs --sql` path would have reported nine live classes as absent. It warns loudly when read through the CLI; a consumer piping the JSON or querying the file directly sees no warning at all. Second instance, produced while diagnosing another class: a session read a failure list from a suite run that had started thirty minutes earlier, attributed six dangling import pairs from it, and five of the six had already been repaired by peers before it looked. The downstream cost of that same stale projection, measured rather than predicted: a session reading P4 and M2 through it found them "barer than they are", nearly filed evidence onto rows that already carried instances, and caught it only by re-reading the live JSON. The registry moved 188 to 195 classes in the few hours between one session's first read and the rebuild. Two instances, 2026-09-24. An improvement-loop pass excluded three sitemap backlog items as blocked because their entries read 'depends: B2' and 'depends: B3', while the same backlog recorded B2 and B3 as DONE a few lines above; the dependency note was true when written and was used without re-reading its target, and a review agent caught it. A vscode-skills plan listed all four tasks of a history rewrite as pending after three had run, and an evaluation agent reported the rewrite as about to happen. Measured by reporter #1 2026-09-24.
classes.analogy: A timetable is read on the platform after the schedule changed at midnight.
classes.scoreBasis: discipline only: re-run before believing WIDENED at ed.13: a proof-state enum (proven-both-ways / pass-only / unproven) is written from two real observations and read by a gate as a present fact, with no timestamp anywhere in the record shape — so the previous wording, which required a measurement timestamp, excluded the case on a technicality. The invalidator is not elapsed time either: the claim goes stale the instant someone renames the runner’s test file or edits its assertion, which may be seconds or never, so a max-age bound is the wrong remedy. Distinct from C30, where the second witness never observed anything: here both observations were real and correct and the defect is entirely in consuming a true past observation as a present fact. Measured independently by reporter #11, reporter #27 and reporter #13 on 2026-09-02, all three within an hour, after this session recommended that read path in a fleet broadcast WITHOUT rebuilding it first. The projection was rebuilt on receipt of the third report. Second instance self-reported by reporter #7 2026-09-02, who also recorded the adjacent error worth naming: they grepped for import statements to second-guess the dedicated checker's list, their regex disagreed with it, and the checker was right. Second-guessing a proper instrument with a weaker one, reported by the session that had spent the day filing that shape against others. The downstream near-miss is reported by reporter #7 and MEASURED by reporter #14, who reported it in their own close — recorded as relayed, not as 4d's or mine. Two properties this instance adds to the row. First, a projection is worse than an ordinary stale reading: an out-of-date file announces nothing, while a projection presents a stale moment AS a current one behind a warning line that is easy to read past, and both sessions who hit it read past it. Second, the propagation was mine: this session broadcast that read path to twenty sessions without rebuilding it, so the cost landed on readers who had no reason to doubt the instrument they were handed. Rebuilt and verified in sync at 195 = 195; the store is untracked and gitignored, so any session can re-run --build without a commit.

proposals.what: A meta-test over schema/*.json requiring a timestamp field on every record-type schema, so no consumed record can lack an observation time.

classes.name: Instrument non-completion
classes.description: The instrument does not finish, or stops before finishing, and either way produces no findings and no failure, so the absence is scored as a clean run. Two signs of one defect: a scan applied too long, running past any deadline with its marker standing, and a scan stopped too soon, dead with its marker standing and nothing published.
classes.example: A multiline regex scan over YAML backtracked catastrophically and pegged a core for 14+ minutes. monitor/sweep-health.mjs header, measured 2026-08-20: the genuinely hung markers (clientA pid 36023, clientB pid 90944) had dead pids, nothing running at any age, nothing published. The counter-instance on 2026-08-23: a 605-minute healthy clientA run that monitor/liveness.mjs labelled HUNG for about 6 hours against the 4 h INFLIGHT_MAX_MS_DEFAULT (liveness.mjs:29), which a reader acted on. The two together are why sweep-health discriminates on pid and not age. Measured instance where the non-completion was structural rather than slow: a wait loop `until grep -qE "Successfully installed|ERROR" <log>; do sleep 10; done` was backgrounded to wait on a pip install that had been run with `pip -q`, which never emits "Successfully installed". The predicate could not become true for a SUCCESSFUL install — the only exit was the failure branch — and a spinning monitor and a slow install produce identical output, which is silence.
classes.predicate: A run with no terminal record: neither findings nor a failure. Non-termination is invisible without a run manifest.
classes.analogy: The stocktake starts in the back room and either never finishes or the counter goes home at noon, and the shelves go down as counted either way.

classes.name: Instability read as provenance
classes.description: A classifier decides WHOSE a failure is by re-running it, so a nondeterministic subject is sorted by the dice rather than by its cause. Distinct from G11, where instability corrupts a claim about CAPABILITY from one sample: here the sample is taken twice on purpose and the second reading is the attribution mechanism itself, so the instability is inherited by the answer to 'is this yours?' rather than by the answer to 'does this work?'. Distinct from M2 as well: an M2 fact was true when taken and decayed; this one was never stable at any instant, and re-measuring produces a different owner rather than a fresher one.

The offered baseline moved 14 -> 15 -> 14 -> 10 across four consecutive offers with no commits between some of them. Three sessions each read the classification as evidence and relayed it to others before anyone re-ran it.
classes.analogy: The lost-property office decides whose coat it is by asking again tomorrow.
classes.scoreBasis: Three subjects observed moving buckets, by three independent sessions, all against an unchanged HEAD. Gain 3 because the corrupted artefact is an ATTRIBUTION mechanism: a wrong owner sends work to the wrong person and is acted on, where a wrong count is merely noise. Closure 0 — no fix is proposed here. The obvious one, re-running until stable, is a better proxy of the same kind: it makes the classifier slower without making the subject deterministic.

classes.name: Receipt without readback
classes.description: A store returns explicit success on write and no later query the writer can construct returns the item. Persisted and unfindable are indistinguishable because the only evidence of durability is the store's own flag.
classes.example: DISPUTED — the opening instance below was re-measured on 2026-09-02 and did NOT reproduce: the record reported as unfindable IS in the store (id 77035d6c, 1844 bytes), all five tag routes reported as returning zero rows return five, and the same upsert-and-recall path succeeds end to end. What that re-measurement DID establish is a different defect — a write-size cliff at the default 5s timeout, where 500B and 5000B verify with an id in 1.5-2.3s while 20000B and 40000B return accepted-unverified with a null id at 5029ms and 5059ms, which is the timeout firing rather than the store failing. Whether the original record landed late or was retrievable throughout cannot be distinguished, and "readback is not synchronous" and "the write is unretrievable" are different claims. memory-layer POST /api/remember returns success true and the content is subsequently unfindable via /api/recall. Second instance, in build tooling rather than a store: Gradle `./gradlew dependencies --write-locks` prints BUILD SUCCESSFUL and exits 0 while writing nothing unless dependencyLocking { lockAllConfigurations() } is separately activated. Measured 2026-08-14 in clientA/libs/platform-errors (BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 3s, ls gradle.lockfile → No such file), re-confirmed 2026-09-02, fixed at clientA d0f1a88b, after which the same command produced lockfiles of 121, 81 and 52 lines; 3 of 3 platform libs showed the identical exit-0-no-artifact shape. Third instance, and the one where the readback settled a genuine ambiguity: a 5193-byte handoff upsert returned state="accepted-unverified" with id=null, and the retry returned was_update=true, version=2, storedSha256===contentSha256 — proving the first write HAD landed and only the receipt was lost, so treating acceptance as success would have been right by luck and treating it as failure would have redone stored work. A fourth, dated but not reproduced in isolation: patch(1) against a file whose context had diverged printed "patching file …" and exited 0 while changing nothing (monitor/rollup.mjs, found by a grep count of 0 after the reported success). Fourth domain, deploy tooling, repo clientDRemote: `supabase functions deploy` exited 0, printed nothing and changed nothing — detected only by comparing the deployed version, still v52 and 22 days stale, where a --debug re-run performed the real HTTP PATCH and reached v53. `deno deploy --prod --non-interactive` printed "An error occurred: This command requires interactive input" and EXITED 0, twice consecutively. 4 of 4 deploy/apply invocations in one session, where the outcome was checked independently, disagreed with the reported status at least once. THE VERIFICATION FAILING OPEN IN THE OTHER DIRECTION, measured 2026-09-06 by reporter #18: a write to the fleet memory store returned 200 and the record WAS genuinely stored, while a readback written as String(row.experience) reported NOT FOUND — recall nests the body at row.experience.content, so the naive form stringifies to [object Object] and the comparison can never match. The receipt was honest and the verification lied, reporting data loss that did not occur. This row already holds receipts as unreliable in both directions; this is the readback being unreliable too, which is the half that makes a correct receipt unfalsifiable.
classes.predicate: A store returning an explicit write success where no query the writer can construct returns the item; requires a readback probe against the live store.
classes.analogy: The courier signs for the parcel and no address holds it.
classes.scoreBasis: mitigated by session convention only; no code asserts a readback after a write Gradle and patch(1) measured by reporter #5; the upsert instance by reporter #27 2026-09-02, whose three-state receipt (verified / accepted-unverified / failed) is what made the ambiguity legible. The patch(1) observation is dated and NOT reproduced in isolation, recorded as an observation rather than a mechanism. The readback remains convention, not enforced by code, which is why closure stays 0. DISPUTE RECORDED: the original observation is reporter #32’s, adjudicated complete by reporter #33; the contrary re-measurement is reporter #7’s, 2026-09-02. Both stand in the row because the row is about receipts, and an adjudicated-complete finding that a later measurement cannot reproduce is exactly the state D7 exists for. Measured by reporter #2 on clientDRemote, 2026-09-02. The inverse also occurred twice and is worth the row: a Cloudflare 524 over a REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW that had completed, and an HTML error page for a migration that HAD executed — reading either as failure would have re-run a data migration. A receipt is unreliable in both directions, so the readback is the only evidence either way. RE-RATED 2026-09-06 by reporter #3: closure 0→1, gain 3→3. lib/memory-layer-client.mjs carries the three-state receipt (verified / accepted-unverified / failed) for one store; nothing general asserts a readback.

The curating session was reported by ListAgents as name-D [ref-7] (transcript T1) in the morning, recorded that pair in the session roster as instructed, and was reported as name-E [ref-8] (transcript T1) the same day without restarting — while a DIFFERENT session had been operating as name-E [ref-9] (transcript T2) throughout, and is cited under that name in 11 places in this registry. classes.name: Inert corroborator
classes.description: A verdict is formed by comparing two witnesses. The second witness's observation channel is inert — it runs, exits cleanly and observes nothing — and the reconciler consumes its empty output as concordance rather than as a null. Agreement is computed rather than observed, and a null observation agrees with every claim; the more thoroughly the second instrument is broken, the higher the agreement score. The statistical signature is the mirror of the ~100%-failure heuristic: near-perfect agreement between two witnesses is as much a defect signature as universal failure. Distinct from K5, where correlated verifiers make agreement CHEAP — here the channel is absent, so agreement is CERTAIN. Distinct from C13, whose remedy is to publish the subject count beside the finding count: this one's remedy is a liveness precondition, that a corroborator prove it can observe before its vote is counted.
classes.predicate: A reconciler forming a verdict from the agreement or intersection of two witnesses, where one witness can return an empty observation set indistinguishable from "observed and found nothing"; decidable by running the corroborating witness against a subject known to contain what it looks for and asserting, before any comparison runs, a result PROPORTIONATE to a lower bound derived independently of both sides. Non-emptiness is not enough: a witness can return a handful of rows where the input demands thousands, and a liveness check that asks only whether it observed anything passes it.
classes.example: A runtime dataflow witness built as a module preload. Measured 2026-09-02 before any code was written: --import intercepts a default import and MISSES a named import of a builtin, because importing a builtin instantiates its ESM facade and freezes the named bindings; the named form is the commonest in this tree. The witness would have observed nothing while exiting clean, and every static edge would have read as uncontradicted. -r with require intercepts all four import forms. DEGENERATE RATHER THAN EMPTY, measured 2026-09-16 on a 200-repository COBOL corpus, which is why this row predicate now asks for proportion rather than presence. A differential check graded a subject parser against GnuCOBOL 3.2 listings. cobc -fsyntax-only -t list -Xref -ftsymbols exited 0 on a 426,757-line fixed-format program read as free format and produced a symbol listing with 4 entries, which is byte-indistinguishable from a correct answer key over an empty subject. Across 1,726 witness runs 32 listings were degenerate, and 29 of those came from a repair pass that retried failing files with the source format flipped, so the repair manufactured the false witnesses and converted a loud failure into a silent wrong answer. The gate that works is a ratio against a lower bound neither side produces: reject the witness when its level-01/77 count is under half of a plain regex count of level-01/77 lines in the source. Before the gate the affected files scored the subject at 63.8% item recall; the same subject scores 99.8% once they are excluded, so the degenerate 1.9% moved the headline by 36 points.
classes.analogy: Two surveyors agree the field is empty. One of them was facing a wall.
classes.scoreBasis: Found by probe before the stream wrote code, so the class was never instantiated here. flow/runtime.mjs proves it intercepted its own probe read (selfWitness), a trace lacking that proof is `unusable` rather than an edgeless clean run, and flow/reconcile.mjs returns divergence null — never 0 — when nothing was comparable. NOT 4: the liveness precondition is implemented in this one reconciler and is asserted for corroborators nowhere in general.

classes.name: The degraded path carries the population
classes.description: A primary path and a fallback both exist and both are tested. In the deployed population the primary path's precondition is never met, so ~100% of runs take the fallback: coverage reads complete, the suite is green, and the primary path ships never having been exercised against reality. The exceptional case IS the population. Distinct from R1, where the branch cannot run — here it can and simply never does. Distinct from C13, whose subject count is zero: here subjects are plentiful and the CAPABILITY is absent. Distinct from A16, which is about how a could-not-execute is PUBLISHED — here publication is honest and the defect is the distribution. The one dimension: which branch carries the population's mass.
classes.predicate: A branch whose guard depends on an ambient precondition (an installed binary, a credential scope, network reachability, an env var) that is unmet across the entire population of runs producing the green signal; decidable by counting, across real runs, how many entered each branch — never by reading coverage, which counts the fallback as coverage of the pair.
classes.example: The client-spec intake lane shells out to pdftotext, mutool, pdftoppm or qpdf for PDF conversion. Censused 2026-09-02 on the build machine: all four absent, only textutil and sandbox-exec present. The no-converter noscan path is therefore the normal condition rather than an edge case, and every test claiming to exercise PDF handling exercises the refusal.
classes.analogy: The fire drill has run monthly for ten years. Nobody has opened the door that is locked.
classes.scoreBasis: Observed in one lane. The intake run record carries a required preflight field so a consumer can distinguish noscan from an attested zero, and the memory ceiling records enforced:false rather than claiming a ceiling macOS ignores. NOT higher: nothing counts branch entry across runs, so the population's mass is asserted from one machine's census rather than measured.

mitigations.what: the intake run record carries a required preflight field; the memory ceiling records enforced:false
mitigations.evidence: scoreBasis

classes.name: Comparison over the union of two coverages
classes.description: Two witnesses with different coverage are compared over the union of what either could see rather than the intersection of what both could, so the complement — subjects one witness never examined — is scored as disagreement. The over-report grows with the population, so a larger subject reads as a worsening crisis. Exact mirror of M19, where the INTERSECTION of two declared-complementary lanes is double-counted; here it is the COMPLEMENT that is falsely counted. Distinct from M18: there is one measurement admitting several denominators there, and two sources joined wrongly here.
classes.predicate: A divergence, agreement or delta figure computed between two sources whose coverage sets differ, without restricting the comparison to the intersection and without reporting the uncovered complement as its own quantity.
classes.example: A static dataflow pass reads 965 modules; the runtime pass observes only the 14 that a checked read-only command set enters. Compared naively, an early run scored a directory walk as 2,001 false negatives — the instrument becoming the crisis it was measuring. Separating "path the static pass could have seen" from "path built at runtime" took it to 30, and three further coverage distinctions took it to 0. Orphans went 36/20 to 1/1 over the same corrections.
classes.analogy: Two censuses disagree about a country. One of them only visited the capital.
classes.scoreBasis: flow/reconcile.mjs restricts the headline divergence to modules the runtime actually entered and reports unvisited separately; the four over-reports during development were each traced to a coverage boundary scored as disagreement, and each correction is tested. NOT 4: the discipline is implemented in one reconciler and is not asserted for two-source comparisons generally.

basis.quote: sites in the intersection are counted in both baselines

mitigations.what: flow/reconcile.mjs restricts the headline divergence to modules the runtime entered and reports unvisited separately
mitigations.evidence: scoreBasis; one reconciler

classes.name: Same name, divergent derivation across a seam
classes.description: Two producers on opposite sides of a contract declare a field with the same name AND the same type, derived differently, so it type-checks, schema-validates and composes while meaning the opposite thing. The name's agreement is the concealment: reviewers use name agreement as evidence of contract agreement. Inverse of M13, whose producers declare DIFFERENT shapes and therefore cannot aggregate at all — here the shapes agree and it aggregates fine, wrongly. Distinct from A22, which is one value with two readers inside one module; this is two producers across a stream boundary. Distinct from G16, whose referent is never fixed; here it is fixed twice, differently, both times explicitly.
classes.predicate: One field name carrying the same type on both sides of a producer/consumer contract with different derivations; decidable only by comparing the two derivations, never by a type check or schema validation, both of which pass.
classes.example: A harness contract specified matchKey on two record types either side of a producer/consumer seam — content-only on one, scoped by the source document sha on the other, both sha256 hex. The document sha changes on any byte edit, so the consumer's differ would have silently failed to re-link across revisions while validating cleanly. Caught on read by the producing stream, not by review.
classes.analogy: Two departments both report headcount. One counts people and one counts contracts.
classes.scoreBasis: Caught once, pre-landing, by the reading stream rather than by any check; the contract now states the derivation on both sides of the seam. NOT higher: nothing compares derivations across a seam and no structural check can, which is the class predicate restated.

basis.quote: Two or more producers declaring different shapes for one concept

mitigations.what: two derivations of one field name are compared by reading both; type and schema checks pass by construction

classes.name: Control shares the subject's failure mode
classes.description: A negative result is read as evidence about the subject while the apparatus that produced it could not have expressed the failure at all. The control and the test are alike in the property that matters, so agreement between them carries no information and absence of difference reads as a finding.
classes.predicate: Before a negative result is evidence, the positive control must PRODUCE the failure. A control that returns the same clean answer as the test — on a version, platform or tree known to be defective — has demonstrated only that the apparatus cannot see it.
classes.analogy: The fire alarm is tested by pressing the button on a second alarm that was never wired to the building.
classes.example: Two instances the same day, reaching the same place by different routes. BY PLATFORM: testing whether semgrep's "Internal matching error" (36,037 across a 100-repo corpus) was fixed upstream, the reproducer under semgrep/semgrep:latest gave 0 errors against 1 on the host — one sentence from being reported fixed. The positive control, the SAME Docker harness pinned to the known-defective version, also gave 0, because the defect is macOS/arm64-specific and the image is linux. The upgrade zero and the control zero were indistinguishable and only the control was diagnostic; both runs confirmed paths.scanned == ['eslint.config.js'], so neither was a no-files vacuum — the vacuum was one layer further in. BY PROVENANCE: demonstrating a launcher discarding an exit status, the "before" file was copied out of a working tree that sits on the fix branch, so the copy carried the fix. Patched against patched, no difference, and the absence of a difference looked like evidence about the defect. Corrected by taking the file from `git show origin/master:<path>`; cost about ten minutes and one wrong conclusion drafted. THIRD ROUTE, BY A SILENT FAILURE TO ISOLATE, 2026-09-03: to test whether a trufflehog lint failure was pre-existing, `git stash push -- <paths>` was run to strip the branch's changes before re-running. The command failed on argument syntax — "subcommand wasn't specified; 'push' can't be assumed" — the files stayed modified, and the "control" re-ran the branch against itself. It produced results IDENTICAL to the test arm, which is what a genuine pre-existing failure looks like, and the identity was read as confirmation. Caught by printing `git status --porcelain` inside the control and seeing the files still M; redone in a separate worktree at the base commit, where the failures were in fact pre-existing. The first two routes had a control that could not express the failure; this one had no control at all, and the output was indistinguishable. MOVED TO G26 at edition 17: the 2026-09-06 probe broken by the U+2028 it was written to find was filed here and that placement was wrong, as the session that filed it recorded once a second occurrence five days later supplied the separator. It is not a control that shares its subject failure mode; it is an instrument that cannot be authored at all in the presence of its subject, and it produces no reading rather than an uninformative one.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-02 on two instances measured by reporter #16, who proposed the shape without naming an id and whose artifacts are on disk (/tmp/sg-172.json, /tmp/sg-latest.json, /tmp/sg-d172.json). SEPARATING OBSERVATION against A23, stated before the row was written: A23's referent is the SUBJECT being of a kind the check does not apply to, and its fix is to narrow the predicate. M23's referent is the CONTROL being of a kind that cannot express the defect, and its fix is to require the control to demonstrate the failure before any negative result counts. Both off-diagonals are populated: A23 without M23 is a grep for CSS class selectors returning 0 because the names were ids and data-attributes, where no control was involved at all; M23 without A23 is the provenance instance above, where the predicate was correct and the subject was right and only the control was contaminated. Widening A23 to cover this would have resolved its term silently, which is G16 performed on the catalogue that names it. Closure 0: nothing in this repo requires a positive control, and the two instances were caught by the reporter's own discipline rather than by any check.

mitigations.what: whether a control can express the failure is decided by running the control on a known-defective subject; it is the convention the ratchets above follow (a planted offender), not a gate over other tests
mitigations.evidence: lever triage 2026-09-06: no mechanism in this codebase decides the predicate; held by rating, review or design

classes.name: Agreement used as the oracle
classes.description: A differential check records each side's observation as a VALUE and then asserts the two values are equal, so the property under test is never stated anywhere. Two sides that are wrong in the same way agree, and agreement is the pass condition — the check has no anchor to be wrong against.
classes.predicate: A comparison whose assertion is equality between recorded observations rather than equality with a stated property. Detectable by asking what the check would say if BOTH sides were wrong; if the answer is "pass", there is no oracle.
classes.analogy: Two clocks are checked against each other, agree, and are both an hour slow.
classes.example: Measured in memory-layer (src/storage/mod.rs, column_store_conformance) and caught pre-commit by its own author, 2026-09-02: a scan-ordering check was first written as note("scan is ascending", format!("{}", pre.windows(2).all(|w| w[0].0 < w[1].0))) — a boolean recorded into BOTH backends' answer scripts and then compared. Both backends returning DESCENDING order yields "false" == "false", which passes. Replaced with a hard assert! on the property before landing; fixed form in memory-layer af84a50, whose commit message names the defect. 1 of the 1 ordering properties the script checks was written in the self-cancelling form first.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-02 on an instance measured by reporter #24 in memory-layer, who searched the registry for witness/agree/compar/oracle/differential/identical first, named R17 and M21 as the closest and correctly rejected both, and proposed the shape without naming an id. SEPARATING OBSERVATION, stated before the row was written. Against K5 (quorum without independence): K5's verifiers agree because they SHARE A PRIOR, and its remedy is independence. Here the two sides may be genuinely independent implementations by different authors — independence does not help, because the assertion is equality rather than correctness, and its remedy is an anchor. Both off-diagonals populate: K5 without M24 is three raters agreeing from one prompt lineage with no differential check and no recorded values; M24 without K5 is this instance, two independent backends compared to each other with no shared prior at all. Against M23 (control shares the subject's failure mode), minted the same day: there the apparatus CANNOT express the failure, here both sides can and do express it, identically, and the predicate accepts that as a pass. Closure 0: nothing requires a differential check to state the property it compares against, and this instance was caught by its author reading their own code rather than by any gate.

mitigations.what: column_store_conformance scan-ordering check corrected pre-commit by its author; no general oracle rule
mitigations.evidence: scoreBasis (reporter #24, 2026-09-02)

classes.name: Fixture unfaithful in the dimension under test
classes.description: A test's input differs from what production produces in precisely the dimension the code under test examines. The guard runs, discriminates correctly and passes, and proves nothing about the production path, because it was never shown a production value.
classes.predicate: Make the fixture faithful and re-run. If tests that passed now fail before any fix is written, the suite was green on an input production never produces. The tell is that a mock which cannot reproduce the production format cannot guard the production path.
classes.analogy: The lock is tested with a key cut from the same blank as the lock, and every real key in circulation is a different blank.
classes.example: Measured 2026-09-02 (a commit, bin/test/gate-tests-core.test.mjs): the fixture returned committedAt as 2026-08-09T12:00:00Z while both production callers inject git %cI, which emits a local offset — 2026-08-11T17:24:18+09:30. The code under test COMPARES timestamps, so the mock diverged from production in exactly the dimension being compared. The guard matched, discriminated correctly, and passed. Making the fixture faithful turned five tests red before a line of the fix was written.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-02 on an argument made by reporter #11, who was offered C26 and A23 for it and refused both with reasons that hold. Against C26 (a guard that runs and matches nothing): their test made real assertions and they held — there is no empty result and no clean-zero signature. Against A23 (output identical for defect-present and subject-not-of-this-kind): the check was applicable and did discriminate. In both of those the PREDICATE is broken; here the predicate is correct and the INPUT is unrepresentative, which is a different layer and a different fix — make the fixture faithful, rather than narrow or repair the check. Related to M23 (control shares the subject's failure mode) and distinct from it: M23's apparatus cannot express the failure at all, where this apparatus works perfectly on a value that never occurs. Closure 0: nothing requires a fixture to be derived from, or checked against, a production sample.

mitigations.what: fixture faithfulness is decided against a production sample the tree does not hold for most producers
mitigations.evidence: lever triage 2026-09-06: no mechanism in this codebase decides the predicate; held by rating, review or design

classes.name: Verification scoped narrower than the claim it supports
classes.description: A check is run, passes, and is sound — and the proposition it establishes is narrower than the proposition it is then used to support. Nothing in the result announces the gap, because the check did exactly what it says and the widening happened in the reading.
classes.predicate: State what the check would still permit. If the answer includes the failure the claim excludes, the verification is narrower than the claim. Detectable by writing the passing result and the asserted conclusion as two sentences and asking whether the first entails the second.
classes.analogy: The door is confirmed locked and the claim made is that the building is secure.
classes.example: Three instances, two sessions, one day. A --settings seam was requested, landed and confirmed present, and its arrival was treated as meaning a permission profile could be enforced — but --settings MERGES ("load additional settings from"), so an empty allow list does not displace 1,156 inherited rules and enforcement needs --setting-sources; the check passed on the narrower proposition. A vm.SourceTextModule probe returned 23 correct static specifiers for one file and was asserted to cover "static from, side-effect import, dynamic import() with a literal, export … from, all exact" — the dynamic clause is false by construction, and a peer measuring 50 dynamic imports in the same tree caught it by diffing two extractors rather than trusting the better one. The third is the same shape in the same hour as the first. | overwatch-layer (reported by reporter #38, own transcript, 2026-08-29 measured / 2026-09-03 filed): claim under verification was 'the sealed deep-link route resolves within a 25s window'; the check run was Chrome --headless=new --dump-dom --timeout=25000, which snapshots at the page LOAD event (~1s) — --timeout caps hangs, it does not extend observation. Four consecutive probes photographed the synchronous cold state and were read as 12-25s state; one diagnostic round was burned on a 'contradiction' that was two truthful photographs of different instants. Instrument-imposed narrowing (flag semantics), not chosen scope — same predicate. Repair landed with the instance: overwatch-layer tools/probe-route.mjs (dd749e2) waits wall-clock then Runtime.evaluates, and its header states the limit the old instrument hid. Fourth instance, another repo (clientD / Portll-clientDRemote, reporter #30, 2026-09-01): `" OR " in filter` was asserted against a freshly built query builder to mean the two picks were joined by OR. It establishes only that the WHERE clause contains that token somewhere, and the pre-existing contactable clause `(email... OR mobile...)` already did. Subject correct, proposition narrower; re-targeting the artefact could not have helped, which is what separates it from M27. FIFTH INSTANCE, and the first with a denominator — the four above have none. Measured 2026-09-07 to 09-09 in commitwork by reporter #3. The check: family VI's within-family cosine (0.017) sits below its similarity to family I (0.020), uniquely among eleven families. The claim it was used to support: family VI is defectively incoherent and should be split, redistributed or renamed. What the check would still permit, and nobody asked: that every other family sits at a similar margin. It does — three hold by under 12%, all eleven hold when measured against the whole register rather than the nearest family, and an INDEPENDENT hand-assigned grouping the metric never sees (the STPA loop) coheres at only 1.14 to 1.40. That control is what does the work: it shows the metric carries no absolute threshold, so "0.017 is low" was never a statement about family VI at all. Three recommendations were withdrawn on it. Ruled into this row rather than minted as "a ranking always produces a worst member" by reporter #40, who supplied the separation this session could not break: the ranking artefact only bites when the ranking LICENSES something, and licensing it is the widening, so M26 accompanies every constructible instance while M26 fires without any ranking at all.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-02 after being held for several hours as a candidate with one instance, on the rule that a class is minted on evidence of the gap rather than on a single report. Three instances arrived from two independent sessions — reporter #7 and reporter #4 — and 4d raised the merge question themselves rather than filing three separate rows. SEPARATING OBSERVATIONS. Against M1 (wrong population): the population here is correct and the PROPOSITION is widened, so re-running on the right tree changes nothing. Against G22 (correct in lane, false-clean downstream): G22's verification omits the CONSUMERS of an instrument, where this one omits part of its own subject and may have no downstream at all. Against R17 (repair scoped to the witness), which is the closest: R17 is a REPAIR written to one site's shape, this is a VERIFICATION whose scope is narrower than the claim, and the two dissociate — a correct repair can be over-claimed and a narrow verification can support no repair at all. Closure 0: nothing requires a check to state what it would still permit. overwatch-layer instance known by direct measurement: the same page probed by dump-dom (cold state) and by CDP attach-wait-evaluate (resolved state) in one session; the two instruments disagreeing on one URL is the differential that exposed the window mismatch. MECHANICAL REMEDY ADDED 2026-09-11, alongside this row's reading discipline and cheaper than it, for the sub-case where the claim rests on a RANKED comparison: measure the margin the other N-1 members hold by, and score a grouping whose cohesion is already known. If the known-good grouping scores inside the range of the population being judged, the metric carries no threshold and the ranking cannot license anything. Three lines of the same script, and it answers mechanically what the two-sentence test asks a reader to notice.

mitigations.evidence: lever triage 2026-09-06: no mechanism in this codebase decides the predicate; held by rating, review or design

classes.name: Check passes against the unchanged artefact
classes.description: A verification runs correctly and passes, against a copy of the subject that does not contain the change. The pass is evidence the change did NOT land, and it is read as evidence that it did.
classes.predicate: Before believing a green check on a change, establish that the artefact under test contains the change — a hash, a byte count, or an assertion keyed on a token only the new behaviour produces. A structural check passes either way, and a baseline-compatible assertion passes BECAUSE the change is absent.
classes.analogy: The rebuilt engine is signed off after a test drive in the loan car.
classes.example: Three instances, two sessions, one day. A container image was rebuilt and tagged latest while the running unit referenced a different tag, so a backward-compatibility check (a known count, BONDI = 9360) PASSED by exercising the three-week-old image; only a NEW-behaviour assertion caught it, production returning 227,567 against an expected 489,616. A registry test suite returned 35/35 and 99/99 green against a worktree copy that did not contain the edit under test, because the tests are structural and pass either way. The purest form: a .replace() targeted a sentence that had not survived an earlier rewrite, matched nothing, and returned the string unchanged — the blob was byte-identical to HEAD, every check passed, and the only thing that surfaced it was the commit tool reporting "landed 1 path(s)" where two were expected.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-02 after being held for a day on one instance. The first came from reporter #2 on clientDRemote; the second and third from reporter #6, who supplied the pure form in which the artefact is provably byte-identical to HEAD. Held until three instances across two sessions existed, on the rule given to every reporter: mint on evidence of the gap, not on one report. SEPARATING OBSERVATIONS. Against M26 (verification scoped narrower than the claim): there the check is sound and its scope is narrower than the proposition it supports; here the check's scope is exactly right and the SUBJECT is the previous version, so re-stating the claim changes nothing and re-pointing the check changes everything. Against M25 (fixture unfaithful in the dimension under test): the fixture is faithful, the artefact is stale. Against M2: nothing went stale between measurement and use — the wrong thing was measured at the correct moment. The reporter's corollary is on the row because it is the actionable half: a structural assertion must key on a token only the NEW behaviour produces, never one the baseline already contains.

mitigations.what: whether an assertion keys on a token only the new behaviour produces is a reading of the assertion against the change
mitigations.evidence: lever triage 2026-09-06: no mechanism in this codebase decides the predicate; held by rating, review or design

classes.name: Write actuator alters authored content
classes.description: The bytes on disk differ from the bytes the author supplied, because the writing tool applied escape or encoding semantics to the payload. Invisible in the editor and in review; the file reads correctly and behaves differently. C5 covers the consequence — two instruments disagreeing over one input — but attributes it to the READING tool; D4 places the loss in a re-authoring orchestrator; P13 makes tool choice decide apparent AUTHORSHIP. This one makes tool choice decide the CONTENT, at the write actuator.
classes.predicate: A file whose on-disk bytes differ from the author's supplied content by a transformation the write path applied — an escape-sequence expansion, or the SILENT REMOVAL of a character class; decidable by writing a known escape AND a known non-ASCII control character through the tool and comparing bytes.
classes.example: Authoring a module on 2026-09-02, the six-character escape for NUL became a single raw 0x00 on disk. docs/TRAPS.md records 11 tracked sources already carrying one, where grep answers "not found" (exit 1) and git grep answers "Binary file ... matches" (exit 0) — neither gateable. This is plausibly how all 11 were created. THE ed.13 WIDENING WAS UNGATED FOR ITS FIRST DAYS, measured by reporter #26 2026-09-06: this row was widened from NUL to escape transformations generally, and bin/test/no-nul-bytes.test.mjs asserted NUL alone while its NAME implied the class. Closed at a commit, which gates U+2028/U+2029, mid-file BOM, C0-except-ESC and ZWSP across the tracked tree. A guard whose name claims a class and whose assertion covers one member is the row's own shape applied to its own gate.
classes.analogy: A typesetter silently converting a quoted backslash-n into a line break.
classes.scoreBasis: bin/test/no-nul-bytes.test.mjs gates the NUL instance across the tracked tree, and its own header records that neither grep nor git grep is usable as the detector. NOT higher: the class is escape transformations generally and exactly one escape is gated, so a different reinterpretation would land unobserved. WIDENED at ed.13 by a second instance in the same week, which the ed.12 wording would have missed: the write path silently dropped U+2028/U+2029 twice in one build. In a renderer it turned a regex literal into a line comment, so `node --check` failed three statements BELOW the real damage and the reported location was not the defect’s location. In that renderer’s test the same drop was silent — the file still parsed, the test still passed, and it now asserted that a function escapes a character no longer present in its input. Loud and mislocated in one direction, green over a vanished subject in the other; both needed a byte-level read to see.

mitigations.what: bin/test/no-nul-bytes.test.mjs gates the NUL instance across the tracked tree
