classes.name: Ownerless ratchet under correct disclaiming
classes.description: A shared ratchet reports a breach to every actor on the surface. Each correctly determines the breach is not theirs, correctly declines to repair another actor's in-flight work, and correctly says so. Every individual judgement is right and the aggregate has no owner. Nothing here is strategic: no actor withholds, games or free-rides, and the ownerless outcome is produced BY each actor following the protocol correctly — which makes this the cost of having fixed P1, where correct attribution is the mechanism rather than the mitigation. Every other member of this family involves strategy or identity; this one requires nobody to misbehave.
classes.predicate: A shared gate whose breach notice reaches N concurrent actors, where the sanctioned response to "not attributable to me" is to disclaim and no step assigns the unattributed remainder to anyone; decidable by observing whether the breach set is ever EMPTY across a window with N > 1 active actors — NOT by whether the count rises.
classes.example: Measured across three firings of the commitwork test ratchet against a pristine HEAD checkout within one session on 2026-09-02: 2 committed failures, then 5, then 4, with membership churning across six lanes. The observing session touched 0 of 16, then 0 of 127, then 0 of 129 files committed since the floor — every disclaimer correct. The gate's own instruction text sanctions it: "If it is another session's commit, say so rather than fixing it out from under them."
classes.analogy: Every tenant correctly reports that the mess in the stairwell is not theirs. It is still in the stairwell, and there are more tenants than yesterday.
classes.scoreBasis: Three firings observed in one session with a 100% correct-disclaim rate and a continuously non-empty breach set; nothing assigns the remainder. An earlier draft predicate claimed the count rises MONOTONICALLY and was falsified by the third firing (5 fell to 4, because peers do repair their own breaks) — the predicate now keys on non-emptiness, which is the quantity that persisted. Closure 0: no mechanism assigns an unattributed breach to anyone.

proposals.what: gate-ratchet assigns the unattributed remainder of a breach set to a named session (oldest active) rather than leaving it ownerless.

classes.name: Local-attribution masking
classes.description: A shared degradation produces symptoms that each actor can plausibly attribute to its own work, so no actor ever holds the evidence that the fault is common. Responsibility never diffuses because the state is never recognised as shared in the first place.
classes.predicate: A failure that N actors each explain locally, where no notice of the shared condition reaches anyone. Decidable by asking what evidence would tell any single actor that the cause is not theirs — if the answer is "an inspection nobody has reason to run", the condition is masked rather than merely unowned.
classes.analogy: Everyone on the street assumes their own wiring is at fault, and the substation stays broken for a day.
classes.example: Measured in overwatch-layer, 2026-09-02: two orphaned gate-test processes (pids 92111 and 92307, ppid 1) sat wedged on fixed test ports for 18h42m, degrading or failing every gate run on the machine. At least three gate runs across two sessions failed against them, and each failure was attributed locally — a dirty tree, a port flake, the session's own work in flight — including twice by the session that eventually found it. Unmasked only by a ppid and etime inspection nobody had reason to run, and killed the same day.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-02 on an instance measured by reporter #20, who argued it against diffusion-of-responsibility and showed that diffusion's precondition never obtained: shared RECOGNITION of the state as shared. SEPARATING OBSERVATION against L9, which is the nearer neighbour and was not the one proposed: in L9 the breach notice REACHES every actor and each CORRECTLY disclaims, leaving an ownerless remainder; here no notice exists and each actor INCORRECTLY claims the fault as its own. The two are inverses that reach the same place — L9 without L10 is the ratchet firing a visible breach set that everyone rightly declines; L10 without L9 is these wedged ports, where there was no shared notice to disclaim. Like L9, this requires nobody to misbehave: every local attribution was reasonable on the evidence that actor held.

mitigations.what: two orphaned gate-test processes wedged on fixed test ports for 18h42m and no notice of the shared condition reached anyone
mitigations.evidence: scoreBasis (reporter #37, 2026-09-02)

classes.name: Reply addressed off the wrong concurrent thread
classes.description: An actor holding several peer conversations in one turn answers one of them at another's address. The address is valid and unique and resolves correctly, so nothing refuses the send, and the reply reaches an actor with no stake in it while the actor waiting on it learns nothing.
classes.predicate: More than one pending peer thread in a single agent turn, with replies addressed from an ambient value rather than derived from the message being answered. The messaging surface does not bind a reply to its parent, so the transposition is representable.
classes.analogy: Two letters are written at one sitting and each goes into the other envelope, both correctly addressed.
classes.example: Measured by the sending session from its own transcript, 2026-09-02: a request for a dispatch seam arrived from one socket mid-turn and a taxonomy evidence request from another later in the same working window. Two replies were composed in one turn with both messages in context, and the seam confirmation was sent to the taxonomy requester's socket (msg_id efa8fed2). The recipient had no panel and no involvement, verified against its own touch ledger; the session that had asked for the seam did not learn it had landed until redelivery. | Sender-side detection mechanism with one measured instance (reporter #38, 2026-09-01→02): where a shared claim registry exists, the sender can self-check before attributing work — query the registry with the dirty set (overwatch-layer: file_owners — git knows the paths are dirty, the vscode-skills knows who claims them, only the join answers whose). Another task holds the path → address that task's session; NO claim → the outbound message must become a broadcast question, never an assertion about the recipient's work. Instance: reporter #41 asked reporter #38 whether vscode-skills test dirt was theirs; the recipient's file_owners query returned no live claim, converting misattribution into 'reads unowned' — the identical query at the SENDING end would have prevented the misaddress. PARTIAL closure only: no-claim ≠ nobody's (overwatch-layer b51bdb0: a claim releases when its task completes and the edit outlives it), so the mechanism is sender-detectable-within-claim-coverage and the residue is exactly the claim-lifetime gap. closure/gain deliberately not changed — curator's call.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-02. The sending session, reporter #20, named the mechanism from its own transcript AFTER declining to claim it as the observed-failure half of L8 that it had been offered — no name resolution was involved, the address was a raw socket, and the transposition was between two concurrent threads. SEPARATING OBSERVATION against L8: L8's identifier is ambiguous and the routing is therefore undecidable; here the identifier is unique, correct, and resolves to exactly the actor named — the wrong one was chosen. Against L7: nothing is asserted or accepted about identity. The recipient was the one able to detect it, because only the recipient can see that a report concerns work it has never touched, which makes this a class the sender cannot self-check. The stated fix is reply-binding: a reply derived from the message being answered rather than from any address in scope. Sender-side mechanism evidenced by the a8↔reporter #38 exchange resolving on a file_owners query; bounded by b51bdb0's documented claim-lifetime gap.

mitigations.what: file_owners lets a sender self-check attribution against live claims before naming a recipient; bounded by the documented claim-lifetime gap (b51bdb0)
mitigations.evidence: scoreBasis: the a8↔reporter #38 exchange resolved on a file_owners query

classes.name: Private workaround disarms the shared repair
classes.description: An actor recognises a shared defect, routes around it locally at low cost, and by doing so removes the pressure that would have produced the report or the fix. The intention to escalate survives as a note; the escalation does not. Every other actor meets the defect with no sign that it is known.
classes.predicate: After routing around a defect that is not yours alone, ask who else will meet it and what would now tell them it is known. If the answer is a note in your own commit message or an entry in a file only you read, the repair has been disarmed rather than deferred.
classes.analogy: The step that trips people is stepped over daily by everyone who knows about it, and it is reported by nobody.
classes.example: Two instances, two sessions, one day, both self-reported. A live one: a scanner pin carries a genuine upstream regression that aborts whole runs, diagnosed to a stack frame and established to fire only under a development default the machine ships. It was fixed locally by invoking the tool through an option that disables that default, with "upstream should still hear about it" written into a commit message and an install catalog. The report has not been filed, the workaround is cheap and permanent and invisible, and every other machine installing that pin hits the same abort with no clue it is known. The second: a session hit a stale-projection warning, read the source file directly instead of rebuilding, and named the consequence itself as leaving the trap armed for the next session — which a third session then hit, nearly filing evidence onto rows that already carried it.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-02 on instances from reporter #6 and reporter #7, both of whom reported themselves as the actor rather than observing it in another. Held for several hours until the second arrived. SEPARATING OBSERVATIONS. Against L10 (local-attribution masking): there the shared condition is never RECOGNISED, and each actor explains the symptom locally; here it is recognised, correctly diagnosed, and deliberately routed around. Against L9 (ownerless ratchet under correct disclaiming): there every actor correctly declines to own a breach that is not theirs; here one actor CAN own the repair, knows it, and is relieved of the motive by its own fix. Against L3: no convention is invented. The distinguishing property is that the workaround's cheapness is what causes the harm — an expensive workaround would have forced the escalation. Closure 0: nothing in the fleet converts a local mitigation into a shared record, and both reporters wrote the intention down in a place that reaches nobody who needs it.

mitigations.what: whether a workaround reached the people who need it is a fact about readers, not files
mitigations.evidence: lever triage 2026-09-06: no mechanism in this codebase decides the predicate; held by rating, review or design

classes.name: One-way relation published as coverage
classes.description: A system publishes coverage over a relation that runs in two directions and implements only one. The forward half is built, tested and reported; the converse has no implementation, no store, no surface and no reader, so the class of finding only it could produce is not missing from the report — it is unrepresentable in it. The published number then reads as THE coverage figure while answering half the question. Distinct from R6, which is decided by enumerating surfaces that exist and counting invocations: here there is no surface to enumerate, and zero throughput and zero implementation are different states of which only the first is countable. Distinct from G7, which has a writer and no reader — this has neither. Distinct from C13, whose scan RAN and enumerated zero subjects: C13’s remedy is to publish the subject count beside the finding count, which cannot be done here because no scan for that direction exists to have a subject count. The tell is not in the output at all; it is that nobody has stated the converse query in words.
classes.predicate: A published coverage, traceability or reconciliation claim over a relation R(a,b) where the implementation computes R but not its converse, and no artefact exists for the converse to be enumerated or counted. Decidable by writing the converse query as a sentence and searching the tree for any code path that answers it — a search returning nothing is the POSITIVE result, which is why it must be a named search rather than a scan.
classes.example: Measured 2026-09-02 building a requirement-chain module. Its own contract names the gap: file-to-requirement is called "the direction nobody builds". The live instance is a fleet file-state module where 5 of 7 states are computed and two are sealed as NOT DERIVABLE, its own comment warning that the tempting "needs specification = built minus specified" over an empty specified set is all 656 files. In the reverse trace as built, a 2-file population with zero markers yields 2 unknown and 0 uncovered; the naive implementation yields 2 uncovered — a finding on 100% of the population.
classes.analogy: A library that can tell you every book on a shelf and cannot tell you which shelf a book is on.
classes.scoreBasis: The converse is built and tested in the module that found the class: the tracer computes file-to-requirement alongside requirement-to-file, keeps three states with unknown never folded into either neighbour, and a whole-population guard reports unknown rather than a finding when no file in the declared population carries a marker. NOT higher: it is one module, nothing in the fleet asserts for any other published coverage figure that its converse was even considered, and the sealed file-state tab is the same gap still open in the product.

mitigations.what: the tracer computes both directions of the requirement relation and keeps three states with unknown never folded
mitigations.evidence: scoreBasis; one module

classes.name: Content-keyed identity
classes.description: A record's identity is assigned by matching its CONTENT against existing records — an exact content hash, or a similarity score above a threshold. Rewriting the content is then indistinguishable from deleting one record and creating another, and the tool performs that delete-and-create silently, as an ordinary successful run. Distinct from C29, and this is the discriminator that matters: C29 is repairable by a better key. A path moves and the file's content stays, so rename detection recovers the identity; C4 is the same shape one level down, where a line moves and the place stays. Both have something stable to fall back on inside the key. Content-keyed identity has none — when the moving thing IS the content, normalisation buys only the cosmetic cases (whitespace, case, unicode composition) and a genuine reword is movement by definition. The remedy is therefore not a better key but a change of AUTHORITY: the matcher may propose a link and must never assign one. That makes this the only member of the family whose repair is a refusal rather than a redesign.
classes.predicate: An identity assignment, merge or supersede decision derived from a content hash or a similarity score over record text, applied without confirmation from outside the matcher. Decidable by rewording one record between two runs and checking whether its identifier survives: if a reword produces a new identifier, or one removal plus one addition, the identity is content-keyed.
classes.example: Measured 2026-09-02 in a requirement differ. Reword detection is Dice over character trigrams, threshold 0.62, ambiguity margin 0.08. Run as an argmax it assigns on the best score and always returns something, so it can never say "I do not know": across two revisions of one requirement, "must support Google and Apple sign-in" to "sign in" scores above threshold, and an auto-relinking differ writes 1 removed + 1 added — a delete-and-create of an id the contract calls immortal, from a two-character edit. As built the same input yields one reworded PROPOSAL, unconfirmed; the store refuses every unconfirmed proposal, and refuses ambiguous or unmatched outright even when confirmed, because those need resolution rather than approval. Ties within the margin emit ambiguous naming both candidates rather than picking either.
classes.analogy: A registrar who decides you are a new person because you changed your name.
classes.scoreBasis: The differ proposes and cannot assign: confirmation requires a named confirmer, the store refuses a supersedes edge without one, and a round-trip test proves an id survives a reword end to end — 1 requirement in, 1 out, id unchanged, nothing minted. NOT 4: this is one differ in one module, and the guard is against the MATCHER assigning — nothing prevents a future caller computing its own similarity and writing the store directly, because the store’s refusal keys on the missing confirmation rather than on the provenance of the proposal.

basis.quote: A finding is keyed on something that moves, so movement reads as a state change.
A finding is keyed on its file PATH

mitigations.what: the differ proposes and cannot assign; a supersedes edge needs a named confirmer; round-trip test pins id survival
mitigations.evidence: scoreBasis; one differ

classes.name: Denominator outside the consumed artefact
classes.description: A tool serialises only positive results into the artefact its automation consumes, and reports what it examined on a different channel. An empty result set is therefore byte-identical for "read everything, found nothing" and "read nothing", and no consumer of that artefact can tell the two apart however carefully it parses.
classes.predicate: Ask where the count of subjects EXAMINED appears in the artefact the automation reads. If it appears only on stderr, in a human table, or in a log the consumer does not capture, coverage and cleanliness are indistinguishable downstream by construction.
classes.analogy: The inspector files a list of the faults found and mentions how many rooms were entered on the way out of the building.
classes.example: Measured 2026-09-02 over three composer.lock files: osv-scanner 2.5.0 serialises only packages that HAVE vulnerabilities into results[].packages[], so two repos returned empty arrays and were nearly reported as having no coverage. The scanner's own stderr carried the denominator — "Scanned … and found 36 packages" — and the table format printed "No issues found". Actual state: 36, 132 and 222 packages read, one advisory total. The JSON was correct and unreadable, and the two channels carrying the denominator are the two an automated consumer does not parse. THE INVERSION, measured 2026-09-02 on scalafmt 3.8.1 while wiring the build-health format lane: `scalafmt --test` puts the per-file diffs on STDERR and only `error: --test failed` on stdout — 21 bytes out, 851 bytes err, both `+++ b/` headers on err, exit 1. A stdout-only consumer gets a non-zero exit and ZERO parseable records, which foldFormat correctly folds to `unreadable`, so every unformatted Scala repository in the fleet would have reported unreadable rather than a count. Same channel split, opposite half displaced: osv-scanner keeps the findings and loses the denominator, producing a false CLEAN; scalafmt keeps the verdict and loses the findings, producing a false GREY. The remedy differs with it — osv-scanner needs the base fetched from the other channel, scalafmt needs `2>&1` at INVOCATION, which lives in the manifest's cmd string where no parser test can reach it. Nothing downstream could have caught it; the split was measured before the command was written (commitwork a commit).
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-02 on an instance measured by reporter #6, who checked four neighbours before proposing and rejected each with a reason. Against C13 (empty catalogue read as clean): C13's subject set is genuinely EMPTY — the scanner enumerated zero subjects and published that zero as a finding count — where here 36 subjects were enumerated and examined, nothing was mis-enumerated, and no number is wrong. Both off-diagonals populate: C13 without C34 is a sweep resolving zero repos into an area and publishing findings:0; C34 without C13 is the case above. Also checked and rejected: C11 (needs a corrupt artifact, this one is valid and correct), C26 (needs a guard that matches nothing, this one matched correctly with nothing to match), C23 (needs an absent subject, this one is present). DIRECTION NOTE, raised by the reporter: this instance made them nearly OVER-report — two clean repos as uncovered — where most of family I under-reports. The class is filed here because the artefact cannot disambiguate coverage from cleanliness AT ALL, so both readings are available and the classic direction is the more dangerous one. Closure 0: the fix is not "read more carefully" — any consumer of that JSON is structurally unable to distinguish the two unless it also captures stderr. A SEPARATE ROW WAS CONSIDERED AND DECLINED for the inverted direction: the false-grey case has two instances (scalafmt, and joern-scan's launcher sending the real error to /tmp/joern-scan-log.txt while stdout carried a 41-byte banner) but both are one rater in one session, which is under this register's own minting bar. Folded here instead, with the direction named, so a second rater can split it later on evidence rather than on symmetry.

proposals.what: Every run record carries the count of subjects examined beside its finding count, and a consumer reading a record without it reports unknown rather than zero.

classes.name: Canonical path shadowed by a resolver setting
classes.description: A control is installed at the location its own convention names, an audit checking for its presence passes, and a configuration setting elsewhere relocates the resolver's search root so the canonical location is never consulted. The control is present, correct, and structurally unreachable, and every check that asks whether it is installed answers yes. Distinct from R1, where the guard's own branch cannot run, and from C26, where it runs and matches nothing — this one is never invoked at all. Distinct from K12, where an ambient value outranks an explicit argument inside one resolver: here a single setting relocates the lookup root for an ENTIRE CLASS of artifacts, so everything at the old root goes dark at once and nothing at any call site changed. Distinct from R15, which is version skew between a merged fix and a running process; nothing here is stale.
classes.predicate: A control installed at a conventional path whose lookup root is redirected by a configuration setting, so an existence check at the canonical path passes while the resolver never reads it. Decidable by planting a DELIBERATELY FAILING artifact at the canonical path and asserting it fires — never by checking that the file exists.
classes.example: overwatch-layer's anonymity pin refuses a Co-Authored-By trailer and was installed at .git/hooks/commit-msg. core.hooksPath=.githooks/ redirects git's hook lookup, and only pre-commit lived there, so the pin was never consulted on any commit. Found 2026-09-02 by a scratch repo carrying a deliberately-failing hook that did not run; the file's presence at the canonical path had been the whole evidence it was working. Repaired by porting the pin to a tracked .githooks/commit-msg, tested in both directions.
classes.analogy: The fire door is fitted, inspected and locked. The corridor was re-routed past it last year.
classes.scoreBasis: The pin now exists as a tracked .githooks/commit-msg, logic ported verbatim, tested both ways — trailer refused, clean message passes. NOT 4: nothing asserts for any OTHER control in the fleet that the path it is installed at is the path its resolver reads, and this one was found by a scratch-repo probe rather than by a standing check.

basis.quote: A correct, merged, pinned fix does not reach running processes.

mitigations.what: anonymity pin tracked as .githooks/commit-msg, logic ported verbatim, tested both ways
mitigations.evidence: scoreBasis; overwatch-layer/.githooks/commit-msg present and refusing the trailer, verified 2026-09-06

classes.name: Control outlives its cancellation
classes.description: Cancelling a control run kills the supervising process but not the enforcement processes it spawned. The canceller holds a correct termination status while the control keeps executing, and the orphan goes on holding the control's shared fixtures, degrading every later run of the same control for every actor.
classes.predicate: After cancelling a control, check whether any process it spawned still holds the resources the control uses — ports, locks, fixture directories. A termination status in hand is evidence about the supervisor, not about the tree beneath it.
classes.analogy: The foreman is sent home and the crew keeps the road closed.
classes.example: Measured twice in overwatch-layer, 2026-09-02. An exit-143 commit attempt whose npm test survived as pids 28899 and 30498, observed for 1h33m contending with the canceller's own retries. And pids 92111 and 92307, ppid 1, wedged on the fixed test ports for 18h42m, degrading or failing every gate run on the machine. In both, the canceller's tooling reported termination — exit 143 and 124 in hand — while the control kept executing.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-02 on an argument by reporter #20, who named L10 and M23 as neighbours and rejected each with a reason that holds. SEPARATING OBSERVATIONS. Against L10 (local-attribution masking): L10 is recognition after the fact — actors fail to see a shared fault as shared; this is CREATION — the cancellation produces the orphan. The two are causally chained on the same pids, 92111/92307, which is itself evidence the rows differ: one mechanism made the condition, another kept it invisible. Against M23 (control shares the subject's failure mode): the control's failure here is self-inflicted by its caller's cancellation, not shared with the subject under test. Against C28 (exit status read from the wrong process), the nearest row the reporter did not name: C28 is the inverse — there the inner process DIED and the caller read success from the wrong stage; here the status was CORRECT and the inner process LIVED. Both directions dissociate. Against M8 (instrument non-completion): the instrument here completes too much, not too little. Closure 0: nothing in the gate tooling reaps spawned enforcement processes on cancellation, and both instances were found by ppid and etime inspection nobody had reason to run.

mitigations.what: nothing in the gate tooling reaps spawned enforcement processes on cancellation; both instances were found by ppid and etime inspection
mitigations.evidence: scoreBasis

classes.name: Fixture the code under test could have produced
classes.description: A compatibility test builds its fixture with the same code it is testing, so it establishes that the code agrees with itself and is structurally unable to express the only input that matters: the bytes the previous version already wrote. The test passes for the same reason an empty test passes, and its name is usually the exact risk it does not cover.
classes.predicate: A compatibility, migration or round-trip test whose fixture is generated by the code under test. Decidable by one question asked of any such fixture: could this have been produced by the code under test? If yes, it proves self-consistency and nothing about the installed data. The remedy is a fixture the current code CANNOT regenerate, which means a pinned byte string of the old wire shape or the persisted layout committed as a golden, never a second test of the same shape.
classes.example: Measured in memory-layer. 4a54053 (2026-09-10) appended two structs to AgentSession under #[serde(default)]. bincode is positional, so a record already on disk carrying a populated context is eight bytes short at that point and every later field misreads: 24 of 9,950 live records, all context=Some, written 2026-08-03 to 2026-09-06, were undecodable from 2026-09-10 and blocked the embedding migration. Recovered at 661d4ec (2026-09-16) with a legacy splice arm, 24 of 24 recovered and 0 of the 9,926 good records taking the arm. The landing commit asserted "Both bincode round-trip tests still pass" as evidence of backward compatibility. They did pass, and they always would have: both encode and decode through one struct definition, so no fixture either of them can build carries the old layout. The two tests are named for the risk they do not cover, agent_session_default_bincode_round_trip and agent_session_populated_bincode_round_trip at src/memory/facets.rs:1204 and :1223, and their existence is why nobody looked further. The remedy shape landed at 6f8bc34, which pins the persisted layout of Memory against a committed fixture so that changing it fails. The belief that made it safe was a sentence one file over stating that #[serde(default)] handles additive forward-compatibility, true on a self-describing codec and false on the persisted one; corrected at 8c02a3f.
classes.analogy: The locksmith tests the new key against the new lock and certifies every door in the building.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-18 for edition 17 on an instance measured and reported by its own author, who checked three neighbours and supplied the decision procedure adopted as this predicate. Against G21 (generator writes its own check): G21 requires the artefact and its guard to be authored in one pass by one agent, so the blind spot is shared by construction. These two round-trip tests predate the change by three and a half months, added at memory-layer 8b82fda on 2026-05-27 against a change of 2026-09-10, which is the measured half of the separation. The other half is a counterfactual and is stated as one: a second author would have written the same passing round-trip test, because encoding and decoding through one struct definition cannot fail for a layout change whoever writes it, so the blindness is in the TEST SHAPE rather than in shared authorship. WHO wrote them is not known and is not needed: memory-layer commits carry one author string across 332 of them, so the record cannot distinguish authors at all. An earlier wording of this scoreBasis asserted a different author with a correct model of the codec as though it had been measured; it had not, and the submitter corrected it. Against M27 (check passes against the unchanged artefact): M27 passes because the change is absent, and here the change had landed and the artefact under test contained it. What was absent was not the change but the OLD BYTES, an input no fixture generated from the current struct can produce. Against M24 (agreement used as the oracle), which the reporter did not check and which answers M24 detection question with "pass": M24 axis is the ASSERTION form, equality between two recorded observations rather than against a stated property, and this survives a hard asserted property untouched, because the defect is the fixture PROVENANCE. Against G15 (fixture from assumption), the mirror: G15 fixture is the wrong shape because it came from the consumer assumption, and this fixture is exactly the right shape for the new code, which is what makes it useless. Closure 1: the remedy exists and is demonstrated at memory-layer 6f8bc34 for one struct, and nothing gates the shape anywhere else.

classes.name: Proxy anti-correlated with its class
classes.description: A detector reaches its target through a proxy that holds over only part of the class, and the uncovered part is not the rare tail: it is the part that looks like work. The detector is correct wherever it fires and has tests proving it, so a healthy firing rate reads as coverage. A gate that matched nothing would eventually be noticed by its zero rate; this one has a rate and a hole, and the rate is evidence for the proxy and against nothing.
classes.predicate: A detector whose trigger requires a condition that is ABSENT from the busiest instances of the class it stands for. Decidable by taking a known instance, surrounding it with unrelated activity that does not touch the defect, and checking whether the detector still fires.
classes.example: Measured in commitwork. bin/lib/turn-gate-core.mjs reportLoop requires runs of consecutive turns that produced text and called no tool (policy reportLoopRun, default 3). Run against the session that built it, turn-gate returned outcome: pass on all four rules, reporting that the longest toolless run was 0, across 263 tool calls in 12 model turns, while three consecutive turns ended on the same unmoved hand-back. The activity is what hid it. Closed by a second rule, carried-handback, which keys on the handed-back ITEM with the hand-back phrase stripped and is therefore insensitive to how busy the turn was: a commit and a commit, 2026-09-16. Over a corpus of 266 transcripts, 4 sessions fire at run limit 3 and all 4 adjudicate as true positives; limit 2 fires on 12 and is unadjudicated. One of the four true positives is a destructive action correctly refused and then restated three times rather than escalated, so the class includes correct refusals that were never converted into a decision.
classes.analogy: The inspector checks the passengers who are standing still.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-18 for edition 17 by the session whose own gate held the hole, reported with two separations and a landed repair. Against C26 (guard that runs and cannot match): C26 predicate keys on a field its input does not carry, so it matches NOTHING, and a zero rate is eventually noticeable. This predicate is well formed, fires on a real subpopulation and has tests proving it, so the healthy rate is the concealment. Against A1 (true alarm, wrong scope): A1 computes a turn-scoped accusation from a baseline-scoped comparison, a right instrument in the wrong window; here the window is right and the POPULATION is short. Against R3 (partial coverage read as full), checked at ruling rather than by the reporter: R3 subset is a filtered one and the record states no denominator, where nothing filters this population and the record does state its proxy, which a reader then reads as the class. Against C19 (completion proxy decoupled): C19 proxy is wrong in both directions, and this proxy is correct wherever it fires. Closure 3: carried-handback is landed and tested over a 266-transcript corpus with 4 of 4 adjudicated, and it is one rule over one gate rather than a rule about proxies generally.

classes.name: Verdict inherited by later members
classes.description: A grouped result is classified once, correctly, and the classification is then reused as membership. Entries that join the group afterwards inherit a verdict nobody formed about them, and the standing entries keep that verdict looking confirmed on every re-read. Nothing that is read is stale: the PARTITION is, which is why a freshness check on the data finds nothing wrong.
classes.predicate: A grouped or blocked result whose membership can change between readings and which states no delta, so a reader can reuse a prior classification instead of forming a new one. Decidable by asking whether the display computes what is new since the last run or asks the reader to remember it.
classes.example: Measured in commitwork. a commit set scopeNotes to a string where manifest.schema.json requires an array, and the manifest-schema-drift failure "every real manifest satisfies the schema" fired for hours inside the gate block of failures already classified as committed and attributable. Counted afterwards: at a commit exactly one check carried a non-array scopeNotes, the reporter own, the only one in the tree; zero at HEAD; 4 of 4 valid now. The block held between 2 and 9 entries throughout, so volume is not the mechanism. A peer repaired it at a commit and a commit; records at a commit and a commit. The remedy is mechanical and the gate already has the data for it: diff the failing test names against the previous run and print what is new since it as its own block, so that membership is computed rather than remembered and the reader has no opportunity to misclassify.
classes.analogy: The supervisor signs off the tray of approved forms each morning and clerks add forms to the tray all day.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-18 for edition 17 from a candidate submitted for edition 16 and never placed. Its submitter withdrew one of their three candidates on finding it was already held and found a second already minted from their own evidence, and continued to stand behind this one, which is the disposition that carried it. Against A4 (alarm fatigue): it fails both halves, because the alarm named a specific test and assertion and was never muted, and the block held 2 to 9 entries, so volume is not the mechanism. Against M2 (stale by the time it is used), which supplies the distinguishing sentence: nothing READ was stale and every printing was current, so a freshness bound on the data would have passed; what went stale was the partition. Against A19 (uniform remedy over deliberate states) as widened in this edition, checked at ruling: A19 runs one member verdict outward over a category enumerated at judgement time, and this runs a category verdict forward onto members that join after it, so the directions are inverse and A19 has no temporal axis at all. Closure 0: the remedy is cheap and named and nothing implements it.

classes.name: Instrument unauthorable in the presence of its subject
classes.description: The construct an instrument exists to detect is one that breaks the instrument own source when it is written there as a literal. The instrument does not return a wrong reading: it fails to parse, before measuring anything. The property that earns a row is that the failure recurred after it had been recorded as a warning in the header of the very file it recurred in, so the class survives its own documentation.
classes.predicate: A detector whose pattern must contain, as a literal, a construct that is syntax in the language the detector is written in. Decidable by writing the literal into the detector and running it. The remedy is that the subject may appear only as an escape, which is a rule the file has to obey in order to be able to state it.
classes.example: Two independent occurrences five days apart in one commitwork file, bin/test/no-nul-bytes.test.mjs. On 2026-09-06 a probe written to find U+2028 and U+2029 across the tree was broken by them: "." in a JavaScript regular expression does not match a line separator, so a String.replace over the probe own source silently skipped exactly the two lines holding the literal characters, the two it existed to find, and left an unterminated regex literal. The reporter separating observation against M25 is that the fixture was faithful and the INSTRUMENT was not, failing in the same dimension as its subject. On 2026-09-11 the non-vacuity control in the same file used the literal character again and produced the same SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression: missing /. Between the two, the first had been written into that file header as a warning. The file now states the rule it has to obey: every pattern is written with a \u escape and never with the character itself. Corpus after repair, gated at a commit: 1340 tracked text files, U+2028 0, U+2029 0, mid-file BOM 0, C0-except-ESC 0, ZWSP 1.
classes.analogy: The note warning about the smudge is written in the ink that smudges.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-18 for edition 17 on two occurrences by two sessions in one file, the second after the first was documented there. The 2026-09-06 occurrence was filed at the time as an M23 instance and edition 17 MOVES it here, because the curator who filed it recorded that placement as wrong once the second occurrence supplied the separator. Against M23 (control shares the subject failure mode): M23 apparatus RUNS and returns an uninformative clean answer, and this one does not run at all. Against C5 and M3: both require the instrument to produce a wrong reading, and this produces no reading. Against C26 (guard that runs and cannot match): C26 guard executes and matches nothing, and this guard does not execute. Against G25 (write actuator alters authored content), the nearest row and the one that has to be answered because both are about invisible characters in authored source: G25 bytes DIFFER from what the author wrote, and here the 2026-09-11 draft used the literal character deliberately, so the bytes on disk are exactly as authored and the host language parses the subject as syntax. Closure 1: the rule is stated and obeyed in the one file that needs it, and nothing gates the shape elsewhere.

classes.name: Lossy transform, structurally conformant
classes.description: A transform that shortens or rewrites content emits an artefact that parses, conserves its counts and satisfies its format rule, while its meaning is a different claim. Every instrument downstream measures shape, so a faithful shortening and a corrupt one are the same artefact to all of them, and adding checks of the same kind raises confidence without touching the defect.
classes.predicate: A content transform whose downstream checks are all structural, where the property at risk is meaning. Decidable by stating what the checks would still permit: if a clause cut mid-sentence satisfies every one of them, the property is unmeasured, and the count of checks is not evidence about it.
classes.example: Measured in commitwork on a comment-rewriting pass, 2026-09-06 and 09-07. Introduced at a commit (bin/comment-suggest.mjs, draftTerse via a fit() helper cutting to TERSE_MAX at a word boundary) and removed at a commit, which replaces truncation with a void. The pass rewrote 893 files, +4,411 and -17,488 lines. Of about 896 rewritten files exactly 2 failed node --check; the other 99.8% passed the parser, passed the terse-comment scan and passed the per-file restore guard while carrying clauses chopped mid-sentence. Specimens published as valid: "// This file is the git", from a sentence about the git side against commit-phase-core.mjs; "// no clock reaches the output, the page embeds src-sha256, not a timestamp, so two builds". Conservation holds throughout, one comment block in and one out with zero dropped, so a canary binding input count to output count stays green for the whole incident. The gate that accepted the corruption was written by the same hand in the same session: the terse rule asks for one line, at most 120 characters and no history markers, and a clause chopped at a word boundary satisfies all three. The pass was reverted.
classes.analogy: The editor confirms that every paragraph is one sentence long and returns the manuscript.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-18 for edition 17 on an instance its author measured, reverted and reported, asking that it widen an existing row rather than mint one if such a row existed. It does not. Against C12 (unconserved pipeline): C12 remedy is a conservation invariant binding adjacent stages, count in and count out, and this defect SATISFIES that invariant exactly at every boundary, so a C12 canary wired here stays green through the incident. Against R11 (no-op edit validates itself): R11 is a replacement that MISSES, leaving the original well formed, and here every replacement matched and applied, so the artefact is well formed BECAUSE the edit succeeded and R11 remedy is already satisfied. Against G21 (generator writes its own check), which describes how the gate came to accept it: G21 names the construction and this names the artefact, and the two are separable, because a gate written by a second author against shape would have passed this output too. The reporter own sentence is the predicate: the checker measures the property that survives the defect. Closure 0: the tool was repaired, and nothing measures meaning across any other transform in the tree.

classes.name: Key not injective over its population
classes.description: A count or a dedupe groups its subjects on a value two different subjects can share, so identical values collapse into one row and the survivor is attributed to whichever subject the scan reached last. One key produces an undercount and a misattribution together and neither is visible in the result. Distinct from C4, C29 and C33, whose keys MOVE so that movement reads as a state change: this key does not move at all, and the same input yields the same keys every time. It is simply not unique.
classes.predicate: A Map, Set or grouping whose key is matched text, a display name or another value not PROVEN unique over the population being counted. Decidable by counting distinct keys and distinct subjects separately and requiring them to agree, which is a different query from the one that produced the number.
classes.example: Measured on this registry, 2026-09-11 and re-measured 2026-09-16 with the file unchanged. Over the four class text fields there are 105 occurrences of the agent-citation shape and 24 distinct strings. A census keyed on the matched STRING reported 24 citations of which 2 carried an over-wide ref; the true number of classes carrying one is 6 (C2, A10, D1, D15, M23, G25), because one token occurs in five of them and survived under the id of whichever was scanned last. Four of six classes were invisible in a result that named two, and the same scan reported both a low count and a wrong owner. Re-run keyed per class rather than per string, the population is 6 and no subject is lost. Second instance, another product and another key space: a batched GraphQL gather on 2026-09-15 reused aliases p0 to p7 across 6 batches, so each batch overwrote the last and 8 of 42 subjects were reported.
classes.analogy: The register keeps one line per surname and the parish holds four families called Smith.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-18 for edition 17 on a defect in this registry own evidence, reported by the session that made it, whose own reading was that it is M1 plus P16 from one cause rather than a row. The row is taken on that reasoning rather than against it: one mechanism producing two catalogued failures with opposite signs is what a row is for. Against M1 (wrong population): M1 covers the undercount and says nothing about the misattribution. Against P16 (attribution to an untouched subject): P16 is a ledger recording an event against a subject the event never touched, where here the recording is correct and the COLLAPSE happens before any record exists. Against C4 (unstable identity), the separation that places it: C4 key includes something that moves, so movement reads as a state change, and this key is stable under re-measurement at the same sha and fails on uniqueness instead. That is an axis the C4/C29/C33 family does not have, all three being non-stable keys and none a non-unique one. Closure 1: the corrected census exists and nothing gates the shape, and the reporter flagged the standing condition behind it, that this registry evidence is produced by ad-hoc one-question scripts no test covers.

classes.name: Ambient rate credited to the change under test
classes.description: A measurement attributes to its subject a rate the environment produces on its own. Both arms run correctly and the difference between them is real; what is missing is any arm in which the subject is absent, so a scheduled job, a background sweep or an already-running process is counted as the effect of the change.
classes.predicate: A before/after or with/without measurement taken on a shared machine with no null arm of the same duration bracketing it. Decidable by running the identical window with the subject absent. A longer window makes an ambient confound worse rather than better, so duration is not a defence.
classes.example: Measured twice in commitwork in one week. The first arm pair read 7 against 0 and was reported as proof; cleared and re-run it read 0, 0 and 0, the original 7 having been the scheduled fleet firing inside a 60-second window. Only bracketing with 45-second idle arms produced signal: idle 0, real 7, scoped 0, idle 0. The same mistake recurred two days later on a different path. Second product, and the arm was contaminated by a process rather than a schedule: in memory-layer the embedder auto-selects LM Studio whenever port 1234 answers (memory/mod.rs:669), so a control arm measured 13 failures against 8 on 2026-09-15, and with the embedder pinned to minilm on both arms it measured 8 against 8. The defence is the same in both: a null arm of the same duration, bracketing the measurement.
classes.analogy: The shop counts the customers the sale brought in and the town holds its market that morning.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-18 for edition 17 on three instances from two products and three sessions, one of them a duplicate submission that arrived independently. A full-text search of description, predicate, example and scoreBasis across the 199 classes of edition 16 for ambient rate, background rate, confound, control arm and null arm returns zero hits. Against M6 (contaminated in the flattering direction), the nearest and the row it was offered as a remedy for: M6 holds the SHAPE, a favourable result produced under conditions later found invalid, and has no mechanical defence at all, its predicate stating that only a later invalidation establishes it. This is decidable in advance by an arm, which is the contribution, and M6 conditions later found invalid does not reach an ambient rate nobody thought to control. Against M9 (ambient-environment dependence): M9 is behaviour depending on an uncaptured variable and its remedy is to capture the variable, where here both arms are reproducible and the variable is the environment CONTRIBUTION to the measured quantity. What carried it past a remedy slot is that it survived one correction, the 7-against-0 reading having been reported as proof before the null arm existed. Closure 1: the bracketing procedure is written down and no harness applies it.

classes.name: Two identifier spaces in one citation notation
classes.description: A citation slot accepts tokens drawn from two different identifier spaces with no notational difference between them, so a reference that looks pinned is well formed, unique and still resolves to the wrong actor. Distinct from L8, which needs a CONTENDED identifier: every token here is unique, and the failure sits upstream of contention, in a bracket that disambiguates a name without encoding which namespace its contents belong to.
classes.predicate: A citation or attribution notation whose slot is populated from more than one identifier space, told apart only by a property the notation does not declare, such as the width of the token. Decidable by counting the widths present in the slot across the corpus, which is a question about the notation and needs no access to either namespace.
classes.example: Measured on this registry. Over the four class text fields, 105 citations carry the agent-ref bracket and 6 classes carry a token that is a transcript prefix in the ref slot rather than an agent ref: C2, A10, D1, D15, M23 and G25. Both remedies proposed for it were withdrawn by their own proposer on measurement, which is why the row exists rather than the fix. Requiring the ref fails because the ref changes on resume: one transcript was recorded as one six-hex ref under pid 94516 on 2026-09-08 and as a different one under pid 59150 on 2026-09-16. Citing the transcript prefix fails because a transcript id is not unique either: on 2026-09-06 one transcript was held by two live processes at once, pids 99699 and 76259, after an editor restart left the old process running, and L8 example already cites the second of them. The surviving remedy is five parts: label which identifier space a bracketed token belongs to; address by the live name plus a ref re-read immediately before sending; correlate across renames by transcript prefix and never address or key ownership on it; use session id, pid and process start together where one identity is needed; and attribute in an example or scoreBasis to the artefact, a sha, a change set or a touch-ledger row, with any session name carried only as a readable label. bin/test/taxonomy-citations.test.mjs now refuses the shape, so this row cannot carry a specimen of it: the row is gated by a test that would reject its own example.
classes.analogy: The catalogue records a shelf number and an accession number in one column.
classes.scoreBasis: Minted 2026-09-18 for edition 17, verified twice against the registry and growing between the two readings, with five of its six instances written by the curator who was recording the class. Against L8 (contended name used as an address): L8 requires two live holders of one name, and every token here is unique, so the failure is upstream of contention and a reader resolving a well-formed citation reaches the wrong actor with nothing to warn them. What makes the row stronger than its remedy is that both proposed remedies were refuted by measurement by the submitter who proposed them, rather than by an argument. Closure 2: bin/test/taxonomy-citations.test.mjs gates the malformed shape in this registry and requires a session annotation on every citation, and nothing gates the notation anywhere else it is used.

remediations.note: D15 was demonstrated three times in one day by this session alone: two replies undeliverable (socket ENOENT, then the name no longer resolved) and one fold decision that reached nobody. scoreProvenance: closure and gain assigned by a single rater, who authored both the classes and the remediations the scores rank. No inter-rater pass. MC-family spread on this repo has been measured at 6.0/10, so treat these as one reading, not a measurement. SECOND PASS 2026-09-06 by reporter #3, over all 199 classes, from each scoreBasis, the remediation register's status text and the presence on disk of every mechanism either names: 28 scores changed, 171 confirmed. Rubric applied uniformly — closure: 0 nothing stands between us and the class; 1 a convention, sensor or one-site fix; 2 a mechanism that exists and runs, partial or unpinned; 3 solved for the population it names, unpinned or pinned at one site; 4 fixed and pinned with no instance measured since. Gain is impact times tractability: 4 fleet-wide impact with a named session-sized mechanism; 3 one of the two; 2 moderate; 1 marginal; 0 nothing on the table. Two rules produced most of the changes: an instance measured after a closure-4 score caps closure at 3, and a register mechanism the code confirms raises closure to at least 2. Still one rater at a time; the two passes disagree on 28 of 199, which is the only inter-rater figure this registry holds. LEVER TRIAGE 2026-09-06, same rater: every class then without a mitigation record was judged for a code-base lever; 5 scores moved, each rise citing the test or rule that holds it.

Folded rather than minted. The proposed class — a repair whose blast radius is invisible in its own diff, a delete side verified only forwards — separates from C24 in principle, but the instance offered IS C24 by the row's own words (a rename applied to a proper subset of its call sites), so it evidences the neighbour rather than the gap. The uncovered region is a clean deletion that is not a rename and lands nothing in halves. A row minted on this instance would split one incident across two rows and weaken both.

The row was minted with a wrong figure (36 days for 58) inherited from a clock reading its reporter retracted an hour later, and with no note that its subject had been remediated upstream. remediationRule: Every remediation declares the class it could introduce. Two of the first two audited items traded a catalogued failure for another one (P2 for R8, and C4 reintroduced by a line-keyed ledger), so a fix with no stated risk is unreviewed, not safe.

operator.controls: fleet configuration, manifests, schedules, rulings, suppressions
operator.test: The defect is in what the operator decided or declared, or failed to, and the system did what it was told.

monitor.controller: the monitor: sweep, rollup, issue store, freshness, liveness, pages
monitor.controls: scanner runs, the issue store, published rollups and pages
monitor.test: The defect is in how the monitor scheduled, read, stored or published scanner results.

scanner.controls: its own run over a repository
scanner.test: The defect is inside one lane's run: what it scanned, how it reported, whether it finished.

agent.controls: the working tree, ledgers, commits, handoffs
agent.test: The defect is in what an agent session did to the tree or its records, or reported about it.

oversight.test: The defect is in how the layer that judges or constrains agents measured, refused, attributed or rated them.

attention.controller: the monitor's publication: rollup, panel, page, handoff, evaluation
attention.test: Judged under the wide reading, where publishing is the oversight layer's only actuator: the class's consequence is a verdict published to the operator that spends or withholds their attention wrongly. Carried only as a non-primary entry; a false verdict published is unsafe, a verdict owed and not published is not-provided, a verdict published after it could still be acted on is too-late, a verdict held past its expiry is applied-too-long.

not-provided.test: An action the controller owed (a page, a refusal, a consumer reading a result, a rebuild) was never issued, or was issued to nothing.

unsafe.test: The action was issued and, as issued, made the state worse or false: a verdict published that was not true, a write that laundered, a fix that re-armed.

too-early.test: The action fired before its precondition held (before a baseline, before a read, before the file landed) and the state at firing made it harmful.

too-late.test: The action fired, or would fire, after the point at which it could still change the outcome: past a declared deadline, after the reader acted on stale data.

out-of-order.test: The action fired in the wrong sequence relative to another action it depended on or that depended on it.

stopped-too-soon.test: The action started and ended before completion, with the partial state read as complete.

applied-too-long.test: The action, or the signal it produced, was held past the point it should have ended: a suppression past expiry, a run past its period, an alarm past its use.

none.test: The class describes a measurement, reading, record or attribution, not an action by this loop's controller; there is no control action to judge in this loop.

controller-algorithm.test: The rule the controller applied was wrong or incomplete even with a correct picture of the process.

controller-model.test: The controller's picture of the process was wrong (population, identity, timing, scope) and its rule acted on that picture.

higher-input.test: A controller above supplied an instruction or authority the controller obeyed, and the instruction was the defect.

actuator-delayed.test: The action was issued and executed later than issued, by the path, not the controller.

actuator-missing.test: The action was issued and never executed, or executed to nothing: no subscriber, no job, no path.

actuator-corrupt.test: The action executed as something other than what was issued.

process-failure.test: The controlled thing itself broke: a scanner crashed, a build did not produce, an instrument died.

process-change.test: The controlled thing changed over time under a controller whose picture did not: drift, moved lines, rewritten history, new rule sets.

process-disturbance.test: Something outside the loop acted on the process: host load, locale, concurrent sessions, adversarial content.

feedback-missing.test: No signal came back from the process to the controller where one was owed.

feedback-delayed.test: The signal came back, correct when taken, after the controller acted.

feedback-incorrect.test: A signal came back and was false or corrupted.

sensor-inadequate.test: The sensor measured the wrong thing, the wrong population, or at a resolution that cannot show the defect.

coordination-conflict.test: Two controllers acted on one process and their actions collided.

coordination-gap.test: Two controllers each assumed the other covered a state neither owned.

coordination-duplicate.test: Two controllers both issued the same action, each unaware of the other.

stpaProvenance.rater: two machine readers per class: one assigning per family from the class text, one blind re-rating a sample against the vocabulary tests; under operator rulings of 2026-08-23 (report is a control action; loop names the reading)
stpaProvenance.method: primary entry judged in the loop the description sits in; attention entry added where the class's consequence is a verdict published to the operator; each value chosen by its vocabulary test; blind-sample disagreement rate recorded in this field by the merge step
stpaProvenance.caveat: machine-rated on one registry edition; where a description straddles monitor and agent the primary loop follows where the example sits; disagreement rate: PENDING

rcaVocabulary.note: Causal edges between classes, over a closed relation set. Every relation was already asserted in tracked prose before it was declared. NOTE ON `basis`: it cites a QUOTE, never a line number. The first cut of this field cited `FAILURE-TAXONOMY.md L615-617`, and two of its four citations had rotted within hours of being written — a peer's edit five lines above moved them. That is the repo's own banned identity form ('never key an identity on a line number') committed by the axis whose subject is causation. A quote moves with the claim it names; a line number names a position the claim has left.

symmetric.test: The edge asserts the same thing from both ends, so both ends must carry it. Validated by closure: an assertion only one end has seen is half a claim.

asymmetric.test: The edge runs one way and the reverse is a different claim. Validated by acyclicity, unless the relation declares cycleIsFinding.

none.test: The relation names no other class, so neither closure nor acyclicity applies. Only a terminal relation may declare this.

same-defect-as.test: One mechanism appearing at two altitudes or in two subsystems. Neither end is prior to the other, and a repair that reaches the mechanism closes both. If a repair could close one and leave the other standing, they are not the same defect.

mechanism-of.test: The subject's CONSEQUENCE sits in its own family while its MECHANISM is the target class — read as 'the subject is the target wearing the subject family's clothes'. Refused when both ends share a family: inside one family the relation is same-defect-as or nothing.

enables.test: The target becomes reachable only because the subject holds. Remove the subject and the target cannot occur. The subject does not itself produce the target's consequence — that is mechanism-of.

masks.test: The subject suppresses the EVIDENCE of the target without changing whether the target occurs. Separated from enables by what removal does: removing a masker reveals a defect that was already there, removing an enabler removes a defect that would otherwise arrive.

awaits.test: The subject cannot be closed until the target is, and neither end is itself broken — each is waiting on the other's output. A cycle here is a DEADLOCK and is the finding, which is why this relation declares cycleIsFinding and is the only one exempt from the acyclicity check.

assessed-none.test: The current closed relation vocabulary was applied to this class and no supported OUTGOING edge was found. This is a bounded negative review, not a claim of causal independence forever; a later evidenced edge replaces it.

unassessed.test: No OUTGOING edge has been judged FROM this class yet. Scoped to the subject's own edges: a class carrying this may still be the TARGET of edges others have judged, and that is not a contradiction. It is an explicit not-yet-looked, NOT a claim of causal independence. Carries no target and no basis, and stands alone.

rcaProvenance.method: Seeded only from causal claims already asserted in tracked prose; each candidate re-read in full and matched against the CURRENT name and description of every class id it cites; a citation that no longer matched the class it names was dropped rather than repaired. Evidence is cited by verbatim QUOTE, resolved against the tree by bin/test/taxonomy-rca.test.mjs — never by line number. A completed review that finds no supported outgoing relation is recorded as assessed-none rather than forcing an invented edge or leaving the class unassessed.
rcaProvenance.caveat: 164 of 199 classes carry unassessed, scoped to their own OUTGOING edges; 11 new classes carry assessed-none after review against the closed vocabulary. Neither state claims causal independence forever. A class carrying either may still be the target of judged edges — M1 is, four times — and that is not a contradiction. THE A2 RULING (2026-08-30): FAILURE-TAXONOMY.md's 'one defect at three altitudes' was a hand-maintained enumeration standing in for a query. A2 was not renamed into something that belongs; it never belonged, and D16 carries the altitude the doc meant. The set is `mechanism-of -> M1`, returning A1, A3, C3, D16 today. masks has ZERO instances, so its test remains untested prose. disagreement rate: not measured, single rater.

commitwork.test: The record names a mechanism in the commitwork repository — a guard, gate, test, canary or tool — and the state that mechanism is in, with a file, sha or register item a reader can open.

vscode-skills.test: The record names a mechanism in vscode-skills — the task, session and claim registry — and the state it is in, or a primitive vscode-skills lacks that the class needs.

memory-layer.test: The record names what memory-layer, the memory store, does or fails to do against the class, from a measured instance.

overwatch-layer.test: The record names what overwatch-layer, the oversight layer of hooks, gates and raters, does or fails to do against the class, from a measured instance.

implemented.test: The mechanism exists, production reaches it, and a test or a measured run shows the effect — not that a module exists.

partial.test: A named half of the mechanism exists and executes; the evidence names what remains.

open.test: Nothing executes: the record is a measured gap or a stated intention.

wrong.test: The register prescribed a change that would not close the class; kept so the prescription is not repeated.

superseded.test: Overtaken by another item or by events; the class is not closed by it.

unassessed.test: Filed and never audited against the code — not open, not done: unknown.

no-lever.test: The class predicate cannot be decided by any mechanism in this codebase — it needs a reader, a rater, a second party or a population the tree does not hold — and the record names what holds it instead. This is a judgement about levers, not a clean.

mitigationProvenance.method: Seeded, not judged: commitwork records come from the remediation register and attribution plan (closes → class, status word → state, R1 excluded as stale) and from mechanisms named in a scoreBasis and confirmed present on disk the same day; vscode-skills, memory-layer and overwatch-layer records come only from what a scoreBasis states a product does, with the sha or file re-resolved in that repository. Proposals come from the register's own REMAINING sections and from the wins the second scoring pass named. Lever triage 2026-09-06 (same rater): every class that had no record was judged for a code-base lever — a mechanism the basis names and the tree holds became an implemented or partial record; a predicate no mechanism here can decide became a no-lever record with the reason; a lever that exists and is not built became a proposal. Four lexical ratchets, two registry rules and one land-time warning were armed the same day and recorded as partial.
mitigationProvenance.caveat: Classes with a record per product: commitwork 150, vscode-skills 5, memory-layer 6, overwatch-layer 7; 36 of 199 carry no record on any layer, and 43 carry a no-lever record, which is a judgement that no gate exists here and not a clean. Proposals stand on 66 of the 181 classes with closure possible and gain remaining. One rater seeded and triaged it from text; a record reads "verified" only where its evidence says so.

sourceProvenance: WHAT `generatedFrom` MEANS, and what its ABSENCE does not mean. Those three documents are the FOUNDING sources. Diffing every class id here against the ids in all three: 0 of 173 source-declared classes are missing from this file, and ~62 appear in none of them. Those 62 are NOT a gap. `generatedFrom` records which prose document a class was derived FROM, and the later editions took no prose — monitor/FAILURE-TAXONOMY.md:36 states families VIII-X have no prose section, and family XI was numbered straight into the registry. A REGISTRY-NATIVE CLASS HAS NO PROSE ANCESTOR BY CONSTRUCTION. An earlier version of this field published that absence as a deficiency, which is grey read as red in the catalogue that names the rule. THE REAL DEFECT IS UNCITED CLASSES, and the count depends entirely on which population is being counted — which is the M18 hazard, met while two readers were discussing denominators. Predicate: a class is UNCITED when neither `example` nor `scoreBasis` carries a sha, a path with a known extension, or a `:line`. Run 2026-09-01: 102 of all 173; 26 of the 62 registry-native; 76 of the 111 prose-descended. A separately-reported figure of ~30 reconciles to the registry-native population, not to 173 — both readings were correct over their own denominator and neither is the number without one. PUBLISH THE POPULATION WITH THE COUNT OR PUBLISH NEITHER. ANCHOR-SHAPED IS NOT ANCHOR-RESOLVING, and the gap is smaller than assumed: of the 71 classes carrying an anchor-shaped token, 59 have at least one that resolves (shas via `git cat-file -e <s>^{commit}`, paths via existsSync) and 12 have none. So resolution costs 12 on top of the 102, not the majority a 13-of-20 hand sample suggested. ATTRIBUTION, deliberately by SHA and not by session name. An earlier revision of this field named a peer session as the source of the correction. Session names are self-reported and mutable, so citing one as authority is a provenance claim that cannot be checked — family IV, inside the field whose subject is provenance. The checkable record is the commit: a commit restored four anchors with each verified to resolve first and deliberately left the rest, since forcing a plausible anchor onto a filing that never carried one is indistinguishable from a real one. SO `verifiedAgainst` MEANS: the declared sources were re-read against this file at that SHA and nothing they name is missing. It does NOT mean every class is traceable to reachable evidence. The narrowing is the point of this field.

evidencePredicate.rule: A class counts as UNEVIDENCED when its `example` contains none of: a 7–40 digit hexadecimal sha; an ISO YYYY-MM-DD date; a path with at least one slash and a known source/data extension (mjs, js, json, md, html, css, rs, py, go, sh, toml, yaml, yml, lock, txt, cpp, c or h); or a decimal integer of two or more digits.
evidencePredicate.caveat: This is a derived reading and it is crude in both directions. It passes a row whose only number is incidental, and it fails a row whose count is spelled in words or whose evidence uses an unlisted extension. Published because four sessions running four unstated detectors produced 88, 92, 139 and 142 and none could be reconciled with any other — a count without its predicate is not a measurement, which is the class this catalogue exists to name. THE COUNT DECAYS AND THE RULE DOES NOT. This field was published the same day reading 88 of 188 and was stale within hours at 76 of 195, because roughly twenty sessions add classes and evidence continuously. The path clause is now a closed, reproducible extension list; under that exact predicate the current result is 71 of 199, one fewer than 2026-09-03 because R14 gained a measured instance. Re-derive it before quoting it; a number carried out of this field without re-running the predicate is the M2 this registry catalogues, committed by the field that exists to prevent an unstated one.
